A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SnapGen-V and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. v2 retains Appendices A-F and adds G-H. Content can be reliably matched across layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench evaluations, mobile timing measurements, ablations, and supplementary spatial-backbone and VAE experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds human preferences, an adversarial-loss ablation, latency results, and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The spatial-backbone pruning, temporal architecture search, VAE compression, and four-step adversarial fine-tuning remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A-B. Removing adversarial loss is a newly evaluated control, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The new human study in Section 4.2 uses VBench and Movie Gen Bench prompts, adding Movie Gen Bench to actual evaluation coverage. Existing text-to-video evaluation, MS-COCO spatial-backbone evaluation, and mobile demonstration coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds an evaluated model variant without adversarial loss to the existing fine-tuning comparisons. External baseline membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged; the new human study reuses OpenSora-1.2 and CogVideoX-2B.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human selection of the best video for prompt alignment, aesthetics, and motion, plus a control disabling adversarial loss. The existing 120-frame, 432-by-768 VBench procedure and separate 51-frame, 512-by-512 mobile demonstration settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 and Appendix G add a direct test of adversarial loss. Table 4 adds latency to the existing temporal-scaling analysis, and Appendix H/Figure A2 adds temporal-block latency curves across input sizes. Earlier data-mixing, temporal-layer, noise-distribution, and inference-step ablations remain.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. The added human-study percentages are point estimates without reported sample or annotator counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values, including the 81.14 VBench total and Tables A1-A2, are unchanged. New results include preference shares of 44.4%, 48.3%, and 49.3%; a 59.44 total without adversarial loss; and latency changes of -22%, +32%, and +107% for 0.5x, 2x, and 4x temporal scaling. Figures A1-A2 add qualitative comparisons and latency curves.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6, latent-space definitions, search action and scoring definitions, and Algorithm A1 retain the same mathematical content. No formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a compact 0.6B model, hardware-guided architecture search, four-step generation, and five-second video generation within five seconds on mobile. The additional evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly concludes that fine-tuning without adversarial loss does not produce promising step-distillation results. Existing interpretations of temporal layers and joint training, and limitations concerning the four-channel VAE, fewer inference steps, and streaming generation, are retained.

D1.justification: Training budgets, optimizers, learning rates, GPU resources, search details, and FP16/CoreML deployment information remain unchanged. Project-page references are relocated or rephrased without a substantive change in access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhan et al., Fast and memory-efficient video diffusion using streamlined inference, as reference 73 and cites it in the existing related-work discussion. Other apparent citation changes primarily reflect renumbering; the paper's research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 corrects stray characters and punctuation in Section 3, relocates the project link, and adds a short user-study paragraph and Appendices G-H. The main section structure and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the user-study table, supplementary qualitative comparison panel, and latency plot. Existing ablation tables gain latency and adversarial-loss fields. Retained figures and tables are resized or relocated, Figure 2's stage label is revised, and the original supplementary Figures A1-A5 become A3-A7.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens validation through human preferences, a direct adversarial-loss ablation, and additional latency and qualitative evidence. The gains are limited by missing human-study sampling and uncertainty information. The new +32% latency entry for 2x scaling is also not reconciled with the retained description of nearly doubled mobile latency. Overall, the additions provide useful incremental support for the unchanged method.
